newsitem.title: BULGARIA: SOCCER-BULGARIA'S PENEV TO BOYCOTT WORLD CUP QUALIFIER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BULGARIA'S PENEV TO BOYCOTT WORLD CUP QUALIFIER.

text.p: Bulgaria's Lyuboslav Penev has demanded the resignation of his country's soccer chiefs and said he would boycott Saturday's World Cup qualifier against Cyprus.
"I will always play for Bulgaria but not while this union's management is in power," Penev said on local television, where he appeared with striker Hristo Stoichkov on Monday night.
Penev, who plays for Spanish first division side Compostela, was dropped for using insulting words on local television after the European championship in England earlier this year.
However, he has been recalled to the national side for the match in Cyprus.
Penev said he was disappointed with the management of the Bulgarian Football Union (BFU) who had not told him he had been dropped from the national side, leaving him to hear about it from the media.
Stoichkov missed Bulgaria's first two qualifiers against Israel and Luxembourg, vowing to quit the team unless the soccer chiefs were replaced.
The BFU will hold a special meeting on December 20 after accusations by some clubs of mismanagement.
Penev and Stoichkov, who is not playing because of injury, were called to Sofia by head coach Hristo Bonev to take part in a training camp ahead of Saturday's qualifier against Cyprus.
Bonev said Ivailo Andonov from CSKA would replace Penev.
